title: Canonical localization comparison for actual derived direct image
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite normed field extension, put $A=\mathcal O_E$ and fix a uniformizer $\varpi$. Let $k$ have positive prime characteristic different from $\ell$, and let all schemes mentioned be separated and of finite type over $k$. Require explicitly that each scheme is Noetherian and finite dimensional and that $\ell$ is invertible in its local rings. On the small pro-etale site put $A_T=\varprojlim_n(A/\varpi^n)_T$ and $E_T(V)=C(|V|,E)$, with pointwise operations; regard $E_T$ as an $A_T$-algebra through the canonical isomorphism $A_T\cong(V\mapsto C(|V|,A))$ of [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction] followed by postcomposition with the inclusion $A\subset E$. Use the integral category $\mathcal I_T=\Dbc(T,A)$ of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete] and its raw scalar localization $\mathcal R_T=\mathcal I_T[1/\varpi]$ of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. Write $F_T=E_T\otimes^L_{A_T}-$ as in [lem-weil-pbc-realization-scalar-functor]. For every $k$-morphism $h:T\to U$ and $M\in\mathcal I_T$, ordinary ambient $Rh_{*,A}M$ is integral constructible and agrees with the specified completed integral direct image. The canonical scalar-extension comparison
$$\beta_{h,M}:F_URh_{*,A}M\longrightarrow Rh_{c,*}F_TM$$
is an isomorphism, natural in $M$. Here $Rh_{c,*}$ is the actual continuous $E$-coefficient direct image of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], encoded in [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category]. The normalization of $\beta$ is that its restriction to integral coefficients is induced from the localization unit $M\to\operatorname{Res}F_TM$ by $Rh_{*,A}$, followed by the extension/restriction adjunction. The coefficient-restriction comparison is the one of [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction]. No properness hypothesis is required.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.2 and Remark 6.8.15: direct-image localization comparison

proof.text: First fix the coefficient identifications and their maps. By [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction], $A_V$ is the continuous integral ring and $E_V=A_V[1/\varpi]$ for $V=T,U$. The canonical charts of [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-realizations] identify these rings with the pulled-back condensed coefficient rings and intertwine the inclusion $A\to E$. The scheme-naturality equation of [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-chart-scheme-naturality], together with the composition isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback], identifies the coefficient structural maps with precomposition by the base-change projection. Thus the two coefficient inclusions and the two maps along $h$ commute. In particular the coefficient inverse-image isomorphisms required by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] are obtained by transporting the pulled-back condensed coefficient isomorphisms through these charts. Use its specified comparison $d:r_U Rh_{c,*}\cong Rh_{*,A}r_T$; $r_V$ denotes exact coefficient restriction and reflects isomorphisms. The module encoding of [def-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-module-encoding] identifies the internal and sectionwise module actions. By [def-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-module-encoding] the integral and field encodings commute with restriction of scalars along the coefficient inclusion, so the isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-module-encoding-scalar-extension] may be taken to be the canonical comparison of two left adjoints of one right adjoint; that comparison carries the internal extension unit to the sectionwise unit $m\mapsto1\otimes m$. The encodings are exact equivalences, hence extend termwise to derived categories compatibly with derived scalar extension, restriction and these units. They also intertwine module direct image along $h$: both sides have underlying abelian sheaf $h_*$, with action through $\eta_h$, resp. through precomposition, and these agree by the scheme-naturality equation above.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.12, Lemma 6.8.2 and Remark 6.8.15; canonical chart and coefficient-change identifications

proof.text: The schemes $T,U$ are qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine], applied to their finite-type structure maps to $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Consequently $h$ is qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1). By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $A$ is a DVR with finite residue field and $\ell=u\varpi^e$ for a unit $u$ and an integer $e>0$: the exponent is positive because $|\ell|<1$ and $|\varpi|<1$. A DVR is Noetherian since every ideal is principal. Each quotient $P_n=A/\varpi^n$ is finite by [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients] and is perfect, with free resolution $0\to A\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}A\to P_n\to0$. This verifies the adic hypotheses used below. In particular localizing at $\ell$ and at $\varpi$ gives the same coefficient algebra and the same scalar-extension unit. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization], the given $M$ belongs to the integral category of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], and it has bounded cohomology. The assumed Noetherian, finite-dimensional and $\ell$-invertible hypotheses are exactly those of that characterization.

source.place: §6.5 coefficient hypotheses and proof of Lemma 6.7.2

proof.text: The ambient $Rh_{*,A}$ uses the coefficient identification $c_h:h^{-1}A_U\cong A_T$ of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image], as [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits] requires; it equals the chart-transported identification of step 1: both are adjoint to maps $A_U\to h_*A_T$ whose $n$-th projections send a section to its precomposition with the base-change projection (reduction modulo $\varpi^n$ of continuous $A$-valued functions commutes with precomposition), and a map into the limit $A_T$ is determined by its projections. Put $N=Rh_{*,A}M$, using ordinary ambient direct image. By [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits], completeness of $M$ gives a canonical identification $N\cong R\varprojlim_n Rh_{*,A}(\operatorname{Res}_nM_n)$, including the specified quotient-tower transition maps. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to the two equal composites of ringed-topos morphisms from $(T,(P_n)_T)$ to $(U,A_U)$. Since coefficient restriction is exact, its derived functor is restriction itself, and this comparison identifies each term with $\operatorname{Res}_n Rh_{*,n}M_n$, naturally in $n$. This is exactly the completed integral direct image of [def-weil-derived-direct-image], with its prescribed tower, rather than an unspecified isomorphism on each level. By [lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible] the latter object is in the derived-complete integral category on $U$: the hypotheses are finite-type schemes over the field $k$ and $\ell$ invertible in $k$, with no properness or algebraic-closedness assumption. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] identifies this category with $\mathcal I_U$, including compatible etale-origin witnesses. Thus $N\in\mathcal I_U$ and in particular $N$ is bounded below.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.9 and proof of Lemma 6.7.2; derived ringed-topos composition also Stacks Tag 0D6E

proof.text:
Write $\eta_{V,K}:K\to r_VF_VK$ for the scalar-extension unit. The adjunction in [lem-weil-pbc-realization-scalar-functor] defines $\beta_{h,M}$ as the unique adjunct of
$$N\xrightarrow{Rh_{*,A}(\eta_{T,M})}Rh_{*,A}r_TF_TM\xrightarrow{d_{F_TM}^{-1}}r_URh_{c,*}F_TM.$$
Consequently, setting $g=d_{F_TM}\circ r_U(\beta_{h,M})$, the unit-adjunct identity reads
$$g\circ\eta_{U,N}=Rh_{*,A}(\eta_{T,M}).$$
This is precisely the requested normalization; it uses the specified $d$ from [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction]. Naturality of the unit, $d$, and the adjunction bijection makes $\beta$ natural in $M$.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15; adjunction definition of the scalar-extension/direct-image comparison

proof.text: Use the $\ell$-telescope of [def-weil-pbc-integral-localization-telescope]. Under step 1's encodings its vertex at a complex $K$ is $r_VF_VK$ and its $n$-th leg is $\ell^{-n}\eta_{V,K}$. This is the same scalar extension as $\varpi$-localization by step 2, and the unit is the same actual inclusion. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-localization-homology-colimit] on $U$ to $N$ (bounded below by step 3): for each $q$, the maps $H^q(\ell^{-n}\eta_{U,N})$ exhibit $H^q(r_UF_UN)$ as the colimit of $H^q(N)\xrightarrow{\ell}H^q(N)\to\cdots$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-localization-push-continuity] to $h$ and $M$: its hypotheses are qcqs from step 2 and the lower bound on $M$, also from step 2. It exhibits $H^q(Rh_{*,A}r_TF_TM)$ as the colimit of the image of the same telescope under $H^qRh_{*,A}$. Both diagrams are canonically $H^q(N)\xrightarrow{\ell}H^q(N)\to\cdots$, because the direct-image functor is additive and carries multiplication by the integer $\ell$ to multiplication by $\ell$.

source.place: Lemma 5.3(1), its common-lower-bound requirement; Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 6.8.2 for the localization telescope

proof.text:
The map $g$ of step 4 commutes with all telescope legs, not only the zeroth. Indeed multiplication by $\ell$ is invertible on $F_UN$ and $F_TM$, hence on the two restricted vertices and on $Rh_{*,A}r_TF_TM$. Any additive map commutes with multiplication by the integer $\ell$, and therefore with its inverse when it is invertible. The unit equation of step 4 thus gives, for every $n\geq0$,
$$g\circ(\ell^{-n}\eta_{U,N})=Rh_{*,A}(\ell^{-n}\eta_{T,M}).$$
Apply $H^q$. The two colimit cocones from step 5 now have $H^q(g)$ as a morphism with identity map on their common diagram. The universal property supplies an inverse morphism; each composite agrees with the identity on every leg and so is the identity. Therefore $H^q(g)$ is invertible for every $q$.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2; equality of all scalar-localization legs

proof.text: To pass from these cohomology isomorphisms to an isomorphism in the derived category, choose a K-injective representative $I$ of the target using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], $g$ is represented by a chain map into $I$ from a representative of its source. Its cohomology maps are those of $g$, so this chain map is a quasi-isomorphism and becomes invertible by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Thus $g$ is invertible. Since $d$ is an isomorphism, $r_U(\beta)$ is invertible; reflection of isomorphisms in [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] proves that $\beta$ is invertible. The construction and the leg identities hold for every $M$ and its morphisms, giving the asserted natural comparison. All uses of direct-image continuity required qcqs only; no properness hypothesis entered.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15; K-injective computation and localization at quasi-isomorphisms

proof_origin.place: Lemmas 6.5.9 and 6.7.2, Lemma 6.8.2 and Remark 6.8.15, with Hemo–Richarz–Scholbach Lemma 5.3(1); explicit adjunction-unit normalization and all telescope legs written out
